content.value_statement: Complex domains can lose clarity when teams mix rules, boundaries, and implementation choices. This skill guides DDD viability, artifacts, routing, and next decisions.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether full Domain-Driven Design fits the project complexity.
Defines strategic artifacts such as subdomains, bounded contexts, and glossary terms.
Routes work to focused DDD, CQRS, event sourcing, saga, projection, and ADR skills.
Connects strategic modeling decisions to tactical implementation patterns.
Lists required outputs, assumptions, produced artifacts, risks, and next steps.
Provides a checklist for strategic, tactical, and evented DDD deliverables.
limitations: It does not replace workshops with domain experts.
It does not generate framework-specific application code.
It is not useful for simple CRUD systems with low domain complexity.
Its recommendations depend on accurate business and team context.

use_cases.title: Assess DDD Fit
use_cases.description: Evaluate whether full DDD is justified before a team commits to modeling and implementation effort.

use_cases.title: Map Boundaries
use_cases.description: Create a starting subdomain map, bounded context map, and shared language for a complex product area.

use_cases.title: Plan Evented Architecture
use_cases.description: Connect domain needs to CQRS, event sourcing, saga, projection, and event store decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Check DDD Viability
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether this project should use full DDD. List assumptions, viability signals, recommended stage, artifacts, risks, and next step.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Strategic Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Model this domain strategically. Identify subdomains, bounded contexts, ownership, language terms, assumptions, risks, and the next specialist skill to use.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Strategy To Code
prompt_templates.scenario: Translate model decisions into tactical patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these bounded contexts into tactical DDD guidance. Identify aggregates, invariants, value objects, events, repositories, transactions, risks, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Evented Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan CQRS, event sourcing, sagas, projections, and event store boundaries for this domain. Include rationale, artifacts, risks, and decision records.

output_examples.input: A billing platform has complex rules, unstable integrations, and audit requirements.
output: Recommendation: full DDD is justified because multiple viability signals are present.
Artifacts: subdomain map, bounded contexts, language glossary, aggregate list, and ADRs.
Next step: start strategic design before selecting CQRS or event sourcing patterns.

output_examples.input: A small admin screen only stores simple reference data.
output: Recommendation: avoid full DDD because business complexity is low.
Artifacts: lightweight terminology notes and simple ownership guidance are enough.
Next step: use direct CRUD design unless rules become complex.

output_examples.input: An order workflow spans payment, fulfillment, inventory, and customer support teams.
output: Recommendation: model boundaries and long-running workflow ownership first.
Artifacts: context map, integration contracts, saga compensation matrix, and projection strategy.
Next step: route to context mapping and saga orchestration guidance.

best_practices: Start with domain complexity and team ownership before selecting tactical patterns.
Document assumptions, language terms, context boundaries, and decision records early.
Use evented patterns only when auditability, workflow length, or read models require them.
anti_patterns: Do not use DDD terms to justify unnecessary architecture for simple CRUD work.
Do not define aggregates before understanding invariants and transaction boundaries.
Do not adopt event sourcing without a clear rebuild, versioning, and operations plan.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan Domain-Driven Design work, choose artifacts, and route architecture tasks to focused next steps.

faq.question: Can it decide if DDD is unnecessary?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a viability check and warns against full DDD for simple CRUD problems.

faq.question: Does it generate production code?
faq.answer: No. It provides modeling and architecture guidance, not framework-specific implementation code.

faq.question: Which architecture patterns does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers bounded contexts, tactical DDD, CQRS, event sourcing, sagas, projections, and decision records.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Architects, engineering managers, and backend engineers can use it for complex domains and cross-team systems.

faq.question: What inputs improve the result?
faq.answer: Provide business rules, team boundaries, integration pain points, audit needs, and any known domain terms.
